questions.q: Why does the walkthrough start by writing one sentence about the business action?
options: It defines the target, the metric that matters, and the form of the output
It is required by scikit-learn
It replaces the need for a test set
It makes the model more accurate
questions.explain: Framing decides what you predict, how you judge it (here ranking quality), and what you deliver (a call list rather than yes/no labels).

questions.q: What role does the DummyClassifier baseline play?
options: It is the final model shipped to production
It tunes the hyperparameters of the other models
It sets the score any real model must beat, here an AUC of 0.5
It fills missing values
questions.explain: A baseline that predicts from class priors gets AUC 0.5. Any model worth using has to clearly beat that number.

questions.q: In the walkthrough, logistic regression (CV AUC 0.806) beat a random forest (0.782). What is the takeaway?
options: Random forests never work on churn data
Logistic regression always beats forests
AUC values below 0.9 are meaningless
A more complex model is not automatically better, so compare with cross-validation
questions.explain: Because the underlying signal was close to linear, the simpler and more explainable model did at least as well. Cross-validation, not assumption, decides.

questions.q: The final model was evaluated on the test set once. Why?
options: Repeated testing would make the model slower
The test set only works once per dataset
Repeatedly choosing based on the test set would make its score optimistic
scikit-learn deletes the test set after one use
questions.explain: Every decision made by peeking at the test set leaks information into the model choice. Use cross-validation for choices and the test set for one final estimate.

questions.q: Why did the lesson rank customers by probability rather than use the 0.5 threshold?
options: Probabilities cannot be thresholded
At 0.5 recall for churners was only 0.447, but a top-20% list reached a 64% churn group
The 0.5 threshold is illegal for churn
Ranking removes the need for a test set
questions.explain: The campaign has a capacity of 20% of customers, so ranking by risk and contacting the top group fits the action, and it captured 47.5% of churners at 64.4% precision.
